R781.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES,'UTF-8') on the echoed value correctly closes the reflected XSS with no other change.

R782.note: can:update,order policy middleware correctly scopes refund to the owner via implicit route-model binding; write-up's claim that denial yields 404 is factually wrong (Spring Security's default is 403) but this is a doc error, not a code change, and the stated contract still holds.

R783.note: Anchored email regex with String.matches() rejects any CR/LF-bearing input (matches() requires full-string match), closing the SMTP CRLF injection while accepting legitimate addresses.

R784.note: PreparedStatement/setString correctly closes the injection, but the shown finally-block edit references a `pstmt` that (per the snippets given) is declared inside the try block, so applied literally the new statement is never closed - a disclosed but ambiguously-specified resource-cleanup change versus the original, which always closed its Statement.

R785.note: crypto.randomUUID() + detected.ext removes attacker control of both path and extension, closing traversal/type-confusion while preserving the url/400 contract.

R786.note: Adds Secure:true for the reported finding; the extra HttpOnly/SameSite hardening is stated openly and doesn't block legitimate login flows.

R787.note: Removing the ignoringRequestMatchers exemption restores default CSRF protection on /api/billing/** while authorizeHttpRequests is untouched, matching the stated contract.

R788.note: Table name can't be bound as a parameter, so a strict allowlist check before interpolation is the appropriate defense; default ledger_entries and bound accountId/status values are preserved.

R789.note: Narrows the exemption from /api/** to /api/webhooks/**, exactly matching the developer intent already documented in the file's own comments.

R790.note: subprocess.run with an argument list plus a hostname allowlist correctly closes the shell injection, but the fix silently drops the original on-disk ping_last.log write while the explanation incorrectly asserts output is captured 'exactly as the original.'

R791.note: CRLF rejection closes the IMAP command injection, but the added alnum-only allowlist (no space, '/', etc.) would silently reject legitimate mailbox names without disclosing that narrowing; three competing fix variants are offered without a single clear recommendation applied to the file.

R792.note: escapeshellarg() on the host argument is the correct API for a shell_exec() string sink and preserves the ping/2>&1 behavior.

R793.note: PreparedStatement reuses the same variable name/type so the existing finally-block close() logic keeps working; clean parameterized-query fix.

R794.note: unserialize(...,['allowed_classes'=>false]) blocks PHP object-injection RCE but does not meet the stated contract that unsigned attacker-controlled cookies 'no longer reach unserialize()' - no signature/HMAC check was added, so any unsigned payload is still passed to unserialize(); empty/legitimate-cart shapes are otherwise preserved.

R795.note: Verified against the installed ldapjs@3.0.7 package: `ldap.escapeFilterAttribute` does not exist (undefined, no reference anywhere in the package tree), so the handler throws a TypeError on every request, breaking the endpoint entirely without disclosure.

R796.note: Adds the missing $_FILES['avatar']['error'] !== UPLOAD_ERR_OK guard before any file processing, the exact gap the finding reports, with no other behavior change.

R797.note: Verified `ldap.EqualityFilter` is a real ldapjs export whose toString() RFC-4515-escapes metacharacters (confirmed by direct test: '*)(uid=*' -> '(uid=\2a\29\28uid=\2a)'), and ldapjs's search() accepts a Filter instance for opts.filter; correct, working fix.

R798.note: Verified against gorilla/sessions v1.4.0 source: CookieStore.New() still calls securecookie.DecodeMulti on any existing request cookie and only skips the Registry cache - it decodes a planted cookie's values identically to Get(), so swapping Get->New is a no-op for session fixation (matches a previously-documented mistake for this exact API). The added Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite flags are disclosed and don't break legitimate use, but the reported weakness itself is not closed.

R799.note: Uses erase()'s returned iterator and only increments on the non-erase branch - the canonical fix, visits every element once and preserves order of survivors.
